newsitem.title: USA: Explorer line delays to remain for several weeks.
newsitem.headline: Explorer line delays to remain for several weeks.

text.p: Explorer Pipeline said Friday it expects to remain seven to 10 days behind schedule for the next several weeks until demand for refined products on its Houston-to-Chicago line begins to ease.
"We are starting our cycles seven to 10 days later than normal. That won't change quickly and we will probably remain this way until demand comes off," said Explorer spokesman Bill Fulton.
Fulton said the 28-inch, 560,000 to 580,000 barrel per day line has been running at full capacity.
"The line is stabilized and we will continue to run at full capacity in May and June," said Fulton.
The delay, which stems from a maintenance in April, has caused some upward pressure on refined products particularly for immediate delivery barrels.
Usually the company allows clients to nominate deliveries for specific cycles, with the option of later switching their reservation of line space to other cycles during the same month.
But since early May transfer of line space between cycles has been disallowed until liftings return to normal and space is available on the pipeline. -- New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631 --
